quarterly_data.signal: AstraZeneca announced (as inside information) that the CARDIO-TTRansform Phase III trial of Wainua (eplontersen, partnered with Ionis) in transthyretin-mediated amyloid cardiomyopathy did not meet its primary endpoint, the composite of cardiovascular mortality and recurrent cardiovascular clinical events up to 140 weeks versus placebo. The company describes it as the largest enrolled ATTR-CM trial to date: 1,432 participants across 130 sites in 20 countries, randomised 1:1 to eplontersen 45 mg or placebo every four weeks; beyond the 57% per arm on a stabiliser at baseline, a further 24% per arm initiated a stabiliser during the trial. Wainua remains approved for hereditary ATTR polyneuropathy in over 20 countries.
quarterly_data.figure: primary endpoint not met (up to 140 weeks); 1,432 participants, 130 sites, 20 countries; 24% initiated a stabiliser during the trial; hATTR-PN approved in over 20 countries
